conventions.convention: Exact real arithmetic; A is SPD on R^n with n≥1. Each prolongation R_i has full column rank and at least one column. Restriction is R_i transpose; A_i=R_i transpose A R_i.
The multiplicative sweep applies index 0 first, followed by indices 1 through m; its error operator has the corresponding factors written in reverse application order.
Condition numbers are ratios of extreme energy Rayleigh quotients for A-self-adjoint positive operators, rather than Euclidean singular-value condition numbers.
Inexact matrices obey αA_i≤Ã_i≤βA_i with 0<α≤β; their inverses therefore enter the bounds with reciprocal constants.

The structured Poisson family assumes Countable Choice, d∈{2,3}, Ω=(0,1)^d, nested uniform Freudenthal meshes, H=√d/M, h=H/n, and δ=q/(Mn) with ceil(√d)≤q≤n. Local supports lie in closed infinity-norm neighborhoods padded by δ+h.
Growth of C_FE(1+(H/δ)^2) is growth of a sufficient upper-bound formula; it does not assert divergence of the optimal splitting constant or actual condition number.

load_bearing.statement: For real SPD A and full-column-rank R_i, define A_i=R_i transpose A R_i, Π_i=R_i A_i inverse R_i transpose A, and B=Σ_i R_i A_i inverse R_i transpose.

For spanning Schwarz spaces with stable-decomposition constant C_0 and synthesis constant C_1, BA is A-self-adjoint positive, λ_min^A(BA)≥1/C_0, λ_max^A(BA)≤C_1, and κ_A(BA)≤C_0C_1. Under αA_i≤Ã_i≤βA_i, the corresponding inexact bounds are 1/(βC_0), C_1/α, and (β/α)C_0C_1.

Under its Countable Choice, structured mesh, overlap and Poisson-energy hypotheses, every u_h∈V_h has u_h=u_0+Σ_j u_j with u_0∈V_H, u_j∈V_j, and a(u_0,u_0)+Σ_j a(u_j,u_j)≤C_FE(1+(H/δ)^2)a(u_h,u_h), uniformly in M,n,δ.
Every Π_i is an A-orthogonal projection with range V_i; ||x||_A²=||Π_i x||_A²+||(I−Π_i)x||_A² and a(Π_i x,x)=||Π_i x||_A².

Assume Countable Choice. On a nondegenerate shape-regular affine d-simplex with d≥2, affine θ,w satisfy ||∇I_K(θw)||_L2(K)≤C(||θ∇w||_L2(K)+||w∇θ||_L2(K)), with C depending only on d and the shape-regularity bound.

For one coarse space and m≥1 local spaces satisfying the stated stable-decomposition, synthesis and symmetric nonnegative pairwise-overlap hypotheses, put ρ=||G||_2 and K=1+2C_1+2(1+ρ)^2. The coarse-first exact sweep satisfies ||E_mult||_A²≤1−1/(C_0K)<1.
If the local spaces span V, B is SPD and x transpose B inverse x is the minimum of Σ_i z_i transpose A_i z_i over Rz=x.

alerts.finding: The reference title says “Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapters 49–54 (complete course notes)”, but its URL is https://people.tamu.edu/~guermond/M661_FALL_2025/chap49.pdf. The opened document is only the 16-page Chapter 49, “Well-posedness for PDEs in mixed form”. The item's locator names “§49.4.2, Babuška–Brezzi; Chapter 50, §§50.1–50.2, mixed approximation and Schur complement; Chapters 53–54, Stokes and MINI element.” These locators do not identify the facet-dual interpolation construction or its approximation proof, and the linked PDF does not contain the other named chapters. This is a source-title/link/locator defect; the Schwarz consumer uses the supplier's locally proved H1 stability and L2 approximation estimates faithfully. Evidence: [Chapter 49](https://people.tamu.edu/~guermond/M661_FALL_2025/chap49.pdf), title page and §49.4.2.

seams_checked.note: The Schwarz definition and local-matrix/projection lemmas retain the supplier's real SPD and full-column-rank hypotheses. They correctly use the Galerkin error projector C onto the coarse energy complement and Π_0=I−C onto the coarse space.

The structured splitting theorem supplies Countable Choice, d=2 or 3, a bounded connected Lipschitz cube and a conforming shape-regular coarse mesh. Its use of the face-average supplier is precisely boundary preservation, global H1-seminorm stability and local L2 approximation; no H2 regularity is imported.

This is a reading-context prerequisite: the downstream page's listed pe26 items contain no citation to the assigned Schwarz items. Its coefficient-scaled interface results are developed separately; it does not attribute contrast robustness or polylogarithmic bounds to the constant-coefficient structured Schwarz theorem.
